title: God Is My Strong Salvation
description: God Is My Strong Salvation in Tonic Solfa to AURELIA, doh is D: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 2 verses and a piano.
about: James Montgomery wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 636 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “Confidence in God. Ps. 27”.

The book printed the words without tunes, marked Sevens and Sixes Double (7.6.7.6.7.6.7.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to AURELIA; any other Sevens and Sixes Double tune fits them as well.
underlay: God is my strong sal-va-tion; What foe have I to fear? In dark-ness and temp-ta-tion My Light, my Help, is near. Though hosts en-camp a-round me, Firm to the fight I stand; What ter-ror can con-found me With God at my right hand?

lines: What foe have I to fear?
My Light, my Help, is near.
Firm to the fight I stand;
With God at my right hand?
His might thine heart shall strengthen;
The Lord will give thee peace.

licence: Public domain: James Montgomery died in 1854.
credits: Words by James Montgomery (1771–1854), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to AURELIA by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
